title: BUNN GRB Velocity Brew 10-Cup Home Coffee Brewer, Black

reviews.title: Best Coffee Machine! Easy and delicious coffee every time.
reviews.body: I needed a new coffee maker and purchased one that I thought would be good. But I ended up returning it because it would not keep my coffee hot. It also had quite a few digital processes that were pretty complicated to set. So I looked long and hard for a great but simple coffee maker.I did a lot of research and finally found it! Bunn Coffee makers are exceptional. If you want great tasting coffee without the bells and whistles, this is the coffee maker for you. It is different than all other coffee makers because it stays on all the time so you always have piping hot water that makes coffee in two minutes or less. (It’s been about one minute for us) I also drink mushroom coffee, which is instant and needs no brewing, so this machine has hot water available all the time for that. No need to boil water anymore for me. Please note that brewing decaf coffee needs a special item which BUNN sends to you free when you ask them for it. This machine has a special spray effect when brewing the coffee and apparently decaffeinated grounds are very different than regular so a different part is needed for best results. On another note, you do have to follow the instructions exactly when setting up the coffee maker. It is not hard at all, but just specific. My husband and I love this coffee machine and because of all the reviews, I know it will last for many years.Read moreRead less

reviews.title: Great Coffee Brewer
reviews.body: Best coffee maker. I love having coffee ready in three minutes. Hot water for tea immediately. I have purchased a Bunn coffee machine for over 40 years. It makes great tasting coffee . You can unscrew the spray head rinse out and ream the line to keep hard water deposits out. They last for several years and it looks good on the counter. I still have my original water pitcher to fill the coffee maker that came with my first purchase over 40 years ago. Highly recommend Bunn Coffee Brewger.Read moreRead less

reviews.title: GET OF THE FENCE, you won't be dissapointed!
reviews.body: I just purchased my forth BUNN coffee maker in thirty years. I hope to get another ten years of service from this wonderful machine! I was instantly hooked on the quality and speed of the brewed coffee from a friend’s coffee maker, I already had trust in the brand after seeing the BUNN name in quite a few local coffee shops so I felt the extra cost over the regular store shelf brands was justified.BUNN recommended replacing the machine in four years so I was a bit nervous the entire fifth year of the first machine but the heating element finally gave out a few years later.The second one came with a pitcher my new mother-in-law loved; she wasn’t use to not having to turn it on yet, lol. The innovation helped her to choose to invest in her own BUNN!I myself was impressed by the valve under the lid when I got my third machine! I only replaced the third one because it started leaking on the counter if left in the open position over night; my home care aide likes to leave it set ready to go for me in the morning’s.My new GRB Velocity Brew machine is identical to the last one; on the outside anyway. I’m left to wonder if they haven’t fixed the leaking valve; time will tell I guess. But it does say they have reached an important plateau in home design as far as looks and quality are concerned.So if you are on the proverbial fence when it comes to the extra investment, I highly recommend you get one! You won’t be disappointed!TIP: if you use municipal water to make your coffee, I have come to use Deer Park bottled water. It is another step up in my morning elixirs quality!Read moreRead less

reviews.title: Best coffee ever.
reviews.body: Really weird learning curve on this coffee pot. But once we got to know each other, bffs. Don't expect the first, second, or maybe 3rd pot day when priming to be hot. It takes a lot longer for the reserve to reach temp than the book says. Fill the reserve. Just wait a few hours or even the next day. Then follow the rest of the directions. I would have sent it back otherwise. Makes the best coffee. A whole pot can brew in less than 3 minutes.Others have complained about overflow on the filters, I just double up. One under the grounds and one over the top of the grounds. No issue ever.Read moreRead less

reviews.title: Fast, efficient, ready when you are, not only for coffee!
reviews.body: We got this on Amazon less expensive than we could buy at our local stores -- significantly less, I don't mind supporting the local economy but not when it is $30 or more extra dollars!.We had a similar unit that we wore out after about 6 years! But we use these coffee pots all the time -- probably 6 or 8 times a day. It stands ready to perform with hot water waiting and I feel we get our money's worth and much satisfaction and pleasure.We start in the morning making piping hot water for our dogs' meals. They get a combination of oatmeal, algae, VITALITY, and a bit of left over meat like a chicken "mcnugget" equivalent (or if we have no leftover use a bit of chicken powder), with a bit of dry dog food mixed in on top. The water is sufficiently hot to make the raw oatmeal (the best for both humans and pets) cook and the supplements mix into the oatmeal and this yields a delicious meal our dogs can hardly wait for.Then it is time for our own session. We have an organic Kona Coffee Farm (KonaComfort.com) and so we never run out and also we never get tired of that wonderful cup or two and it comes out very fast and perfect each time with our Bunn Coffee Brewer. Once it has brewed -- in what seems like just a moment -- we pour our cups hot and then I do not let the burner stay on. If there is left over coffee, our organic Kona is so sweet I can drink it warm or even cold later. It does not waste!Afternoons, we will switch to making hot water for tea. We love good organic jasmine green tea, and the Bunn Coffee Brewer makes the water just perfectly. You can make one cup or two or the 10 cup whole pot -- just what you need at the moment, and it takes about as much time to measure and pour into the top as it does for it to come out hot on the bottom. The coffee pot has a valve on the top lid so that when you open to pour water in, it waits until you are finished and close the top door before it will send the water thru to make your hot water -- this is a nice feature which our last pot (being older) did not have.Later afternoon, it is time for our second pet feeding of the day. And we usually will have dinner about the same time -- 6PM ish, and often will have another fresh pot of our Organic Kona Comfort Kona Coffee.Usually we feel like another cup of Jasmine Tea later maybe around 9PM, and sometimes we will use the pot to make instant soup packets or those nice "cup o soups" or if in the mood before going to bed to make hot water for bourbon totties.All in all, this is an indispensable appliance that we use daily and from our experience will last for many years of constant service.Read moreRead less

reviews.title: I'll bet you will like it!
reviews.body: After using our Bunn for a couple of weeks now, we are pleased with it overall and it does make a good cup of coffee.Pros:  Fast, quiet, and user friendly. Love the fact that it fills from the front. The decanter is truly non-drip.NOT a negative for us:  Yes, as some have mentioned this coffee maker does require Bunn (slightly larger) filters, but that is no big deal to my way of thinking. We are coffee lovers and spend a few extra bucks for better coffee anyway, and the filters are available almost everywhere. If economy is what's important, than one should be looking at the ubiquitous "Mister" brand $15 coffee pot anyway, right?Cons:  I should have taken more seriously what some other reviewers when they say "your whole house will smell like hot plastic for a few days"!  Had I realized just how strong the smell is, I would have set up the Bunn in our garage and used it there for the first several days!  Thankfully the smell has now subsided.  I knocked off 1 star because of this.The only other shortcoming that we've encountered so far is that brewing (only) 6 cups of decaf coffee almost overflowed the filter; I'm sure had we brewed more cups at one time it would have overflowed.  Looking in the troubleshooting guide, Bunn states that if you use decaf coffee OR have soft water, you will need a special restrictor-type spray head.  Well guess what  - we also have a water softener!We contacted Bunn and they cheerfully and quickly sent 2 restrictor heads at no charge. I'm guessing that the reason they supplied 2 heads is that with smaller holes, it will become plugged-up more quickly; we'll see.It's simple to change-out the head, just unscrew it with your fingers and screw the new one back in. And it did solve the problem at least for brewing 6 cups, as we haven't tried a full pot yet.  However, it does slow-down the brewing process, taking about 5 1/2 minutes vs. 3.  That in itself is no big deal since that's still fairly quick. But it does partially negate Bunn's premise on why a Bunn makes such good coffee - that the pre-heated water flows quickly through the filtered coffee grounds so as not to remain in the filter basket long enough for the grounds to make the coffee bitter.  Seems to me that since the restricted spray head slows down the brewing process, water now stays in the grounds a little longer now. And although our coffee still tastes good, it was slightly better with the original spray head.I see that some peeps are concerned about the electricity cost for the coffee maker to have the water preheated all day/night. I chose to put ours on a "smart plug" that turns it off/on.  I schedule it to turn on at 5 am, and then off at 9 am.  The plug is controlled via a phone app, and costs $8 at Amazon:https://www.amazon.com/dp/B091699Z3W?ref_=ppx_hzsearch_conn_dt_b_fed_asin_title_1&th=1I ran some calculations of the electricity usage and costs, using a Kill-A-Watt meter.  Leaving it on all day and night uses 0.84 kWh per day.  We make two 6-cup pots of coffee each morning.  With my 4 hour "on" schedule, it uses 0.38 kWh. per day.  My electricity rate is 10.2 cents per kWh. Other common rates in my state are 11, 12, 13, and 14 cents.  I've attached a table reflecting those rates and the respective costs.  Note that the coffee maker takes about 11 minutes to heat the water from a cold start.  So if you choose to leave it turned off until you're ready to brew coffee, it will obviously use much less electricity.  But for us, and with the smart plug, the convenience of being able to quickly brew a pot is worth the small cost. Hope this helps.Sidenote: Bunn should make the restrictor spray head available as an optional component when ordering the coffee maker, depending on one's intended use of decaf and/or softened water.  But if you feel that you will need it, I suggest that calling Bunn and requesting the restrictor head immediately after ordering the coffee maker; they required no proof of purchase and no product date code, only the model number "GRB".  Phone 800-352-BUNNIn summary, if this coffee maker lasts a few years we'll be very happy.  And if it doesn't, we may buy another one anyway  :>)Read moreRead less
